newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business - April 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TARMAC SAYS NO TO RELAYFAST BID

Construction group Tarmac will not buy Relayfast, a privatised railway engineering business, up for sale after losing contracts with Railtrack. Relayfast, which is backed by Hambro European Ventures and the Aberdeen fund management group Abtrust, has appointed Coopers and Lybrand Corporate Finance to sell the business. Amey, the construction group that bought British Rail's western infrastructure maintenance unit for 15 million stg, is interested, as are Jarvis and Balfour Beatty.
-- ANGLO FACES EU CURBS ON PLATINUM MONOPOLY FEARS

Anglo American Corp, the South African mining giant, may have to reduce its precious metals interests in exchange for winning European Commission clearing for its takeover of Lonrho. The EU's merger task orce carried out a full-scale investigation over fears that Anglo American's increased stake in Lonrho would tighten the South African firms's stranglehold on the world's output of platinum.
-- GAS OPPONENTS CLASH ON DELAY IN MMC REPORT

Clare Spottiswoode, industry regulator, and British Gas have clashed over the reasons behind a delay in the completion of a Mergers and Monopolies Commission investigation until after the election. The commission wants more time to look at Spottiswoode's proposals for tighter controls over TransCo, the British Gas pipeline subsidiary, after she produced new material to try to convince the commission to support her case for a tough line.
THE TIMES
-- JRA FOUNDERS IN LINE FOR 37 MILLION STG BONUS

Lord Rothschild, Sir Mark Weinberg, Mike Wilson and Keith Carby, the founders of J Rothschild Assurance, are set to earn up to 12 million stg each after Prudential raised its stake in the company by 40 million stg. This gives Prudential control over JRA. Under the terms of the deal Prudential has tabled a 39.6 million stg plan to increase its stake in St James's Place Capital, the life assurance and fund firm that owns 40 per cent of JRA.
-- WARRIOR TARGETS ARMED FORCES

Under a 104 million stg deal with Naafi, the purveyor of tea and cakes to the British armed forces, up to 10 million former servicemen and women are to be offered credit cards, insurance schemes and personal loans. A joint venture between Naafi and HSBC Personal Equity, called Warrior Group, has won the contract. Naafi's chief executive Geoffrey Dart said the money raised would help Naafi with its restructuring, and allow it to modernise its pubs, clubs and leisure centres.
-- MANUFACTURING RECOVERY FRAGILE

Figures from the Office of National Statistics show that the recovery in the manufacturing sector remains fragile, leading analysts to claim that Britain is on the verge of becoming a "two-speed" economy. Interest rates are forecast to rise by as much as half a percentage point next month, which will prompt a further rise in sterling. Export demand has risen in recent months, however, manufacturers are starting to suffer from the surge in sterling, with the full impact predicted for later this year.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EXECUTIVE PAY RISES FUEL GRAVY TRAIN ROW

According to an annual report from National Express, one of the companies running large parts of the privatised rail network, Phil White, chief executive, has been paid a bonus of almost one million stg. A spokesman said he received this for his part in a wide-ranging shake-up of the group's rail operations. The news comes after the publication of numerous company reports, many of which contained examples of large salary increases and pay-offs.
-- BLOW FOR FIAT AS TOP EXECUTIVES GIVEN JAIL TERMS

Cesare Romiti, chairman of Fiat, the Italian carmaker, has been sentenced to a year and six months in prison for falsifying the company's books and has been barred from holding a board position. Finance director, Paolo Matteoli, was found guilty on the same charges and received a year and four months in prison and barred from holding a board position. Defence lawyers have described the sentences as unjust and senior business and political figures have expressed shock.
-- SIEMENS BECOMES POWER ON TYNESIDE

German industrial giant, Siemens, has bought most of Parsons power-generation business from Rolls-Royce for 30 million stg and has taken on 880 employees, thus making the company Tyneside's biggest manufacturing employer. The purchase marks the end of Parsons brand-name after 113 years. Parsons will become part of Siemens Power Generation, which claims to rank third in the world in this sector.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- LADBROKE CHIEF UNDER FIRE AFTER 266 PER CENT RISE

It has emerged that Peter George, chief executive of Ladbroke Group, pocketed 1.3 million stg in 1996, a rise of 266 per cent on the previous year. This is due to an incentive scheme for directors, introduced when George became chief executive, which rewards directors on the performance of the share price of the betting shops, casinos and hotels company. John Jackson, chairman of Ladbroke's remuneration committee admitted that the scheme may be over-generous.
-- LANICA PLANS TEN MILLION STG WHOLESALE CUTS FOR CO-OP

If the approach to control parts of the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) non-food interests by Andrew Regan's Lanica Trust is successful he would cut central costs by 10 million stg, introduce bumper incentive schemes for employees and prune middle management. Lanica has estimated that the CWS's central office costs in Manchester are around 16 million stg per year and two-thirds of these costs will be removed.
-- IONICA CHASES BRITISH TELECOM WITH CREATION OF 600
NEW JOBS

Ionica, the telephone operator that combines wireless technology with fixed phone lines, has announced a drive to create up to 600 jobs in Birmingham following stronger-than-expected consumer demand. The expansion will intensify pressure on British Telecom, the target of Ionica's assault on the domestic market. Ionica offers a 15 per cent cut in call charges over BT and 20 per cent lower line rental bills.
